steps.prompt:
INTEGRATION STEP for Product Oracle v1. Read docs/v1-plan.md in full first. Lanes A (members), B2a/B2b (connectors) are already on main. The other lanes' work is on branches of origin: lane/k-connections, lane/b1-sources, lane/c-baseline, lane/f-templates, lane/d1-mcp, lane/d2-mcp-oauth, lane/e-runs (fetch them with git fetch origin 'refs/heads/lane/*:refs/remotes/origin/lane/*'). Each was built in parallel from an older main, and none was tested together.

1. Merge them into this branch in this order: k-connections, b1-sources, c-baseline, f-templates, d1-mcp, d2-mcp-oauth, e-runs. Resolve every conflict by keeping both lanes' intent: route registration in api/oracle/main.py, the generated web/lib/api (regenerate with `make openapi`, never hand-merge it), shared web navigation and components, and any duplicated helpers (B1 and K both read connection credentials: keep K's connections.service.get_credential and make B1 call it). Migrations: 0001-0003 on main, 0004 from d2-mcp-oauth; there must be one linear chain.
2. Wire the lanes together where each one left a hook: register D2's OAuth access-token verifier with D1's oracle.mcp.auth registry; make D1's curated search tool return B1's confidence; make E's runs ingest a segment's baseline.yaml artifact through C's YAML import (locks respected, proposals created); make F's priorities read C's evidence confidence.
3. Run everything: the full API suite against Postgres (ORACLE_TEST_DATABASE_URL), ruff check and ruff format --check, `make openapi` (commit the result), web lint, tsc, build, the Playwright mock suite, and `make e2e` if Postgres and Chromium are available. Fix what fails. If Chromium cannot start here, say so plainly; CI runs it.
4. Write $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/integrate-report.md: conflicts and how each was resolved, wiring done, test results with counts, anything not verified.
Product Oracle words only: one company's Oracle, its users and their roles; never 'workspace'. Never touch .github/. Commit your work.

Decisions to apply while integrating (owner and engineering defaults, 2026-10-17): (a) API tokens can act for a user: migration 0005 (down_revision 0004) adds a nullable api_tokens.user_id FK; a token with a user acts as that user (role and owner) so `oracle sync` and other per-user calls work with ORACLE_API_TOKEN; tokens without a user keep today's behaviour. (b) When a sync gets a rejected credential, also mark the user's connection expired with last_error, so Settings > Connections shows Reconnect. (c) Disconnect also revokes the token at the provider where an endpoint exists (GitHub, Slack, Google), best effort, then deletes Oracle's copy. (d) Keep as built: a run's budget gates only the estimate; an MCP client asking for no scope gets oracle:read oracle:write (capped by the user's role); a run paused on overrun lets the running segment finish and keeps its output; immaterial conflicts apply as agent writes (locked items become proposals); OAuth registration stays open; grants slide 30 days; a resumed run gets 0.5x the estimate more; snapshots pin at start. (e) Do not spend effort on Lane K's per-user Claude plan or llm gateway: a later step removes them (agents and model calls run in SwarmCloud). (f) From lane F: a document with no theme and no template suggestion exports with the built-in default theme (clean-document for PRDs, roadmap-board for roadmaps, with the Sources and data points appendix) instead of the legacy stylesheet; keep 'suggest when' and suggested theme in template front matter; approvers and owners edit templates and themes; proposed 'supports' links to confirmed goals count toward goal value, with their status shown.

PUBLIC-LINK EVIDENCE for Product Oracle v1 (owner's decision, 2026-10-17: 'commenters can attach evidence or supporting docs in the UI via public links like public Notion pages or public Google Docs but will not need to connect their accounts'). Read docs/v1-plan.md (Amendments, Confidence) and the baseline code (api/oracle/baseline/, evidence model, confidence scoring) first.

Build: (1) POST /v1/baseline/evidence/link {target entity or edge, url, note?} for commenter and up: accept only https URLs of public pages (public Notion pages on notion.site or notion.so, Google Docs shared as 'anyone with the link', and plain public web pages); fetch server-side without any credential, with a timeout, size cap, content-type check and SSRF protection (resolve the host and refuse private, loopback and link-local addresses; no redirects to them); extract readable text (Google Docs via the public export ?format=txt endpoint; Notion public pages via their HTML; others via the page's main text), store a snapshot (title, text, fetched_at, last-modified when the page states it) and the evidence row with url, excerpt and kind so confidence scores it like a notion / google_docs / web source (freshness from last-modified, else fetched_at). A page that needs sign-in or is not public gets a clear 'this link is not public' error. Public-link evidence is visible to every user (it is public), unlike items from private connections. (2) Re-fetch on demand (POST .../refresh) to update the snapshot and rescore. (3) UI: on the Baseline feature drawer and on document sections, an 'Add evidence link' control for commenters and up, showing the fetched title, excerpt and confidence before saving. (4) Tests: allowed and refused URLs, SSRF refusal, non-public page, Google Docs and Notion extraction from recorded fixtures, scoring, role checks, Playwright mock test. Run the full API suite, ruff, make openapi, web lint/tsc/build, Playwright. Commit. Write $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/public-links-report.md. Product Oracle words only; never touch .github/.

CLAUDE ACCOUNT POOL for Product Oracle v1, with EXACTLY SwarmCloud's account management (owner's instruction: 'use the EXACT account management functionality as in SwarmCloud; the app is used locally, for experimentation, for local personal use'). Read docs/v1-plan.md section 'Claude accounts' and docs/questions.md row P3b first. Then read SwarmCloud's public repo (git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud into a scratch directory outside this checkout, read only): apps/quota-broker/quota_broker/ (accounts.py, accountstore.py, oauth.py, credentials.py, usage.py, usagepoll.py, main.py account routes), apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/accountlease.py and runners/cliagent.py (rate_limit_event readings, swap at a turn boundary), apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/routes/accounts.py, apps/swarm-ui/src/Accounts.tsx, apps/swarm-mcp/swarm_mcp/sc.py and render.py, docs/account-holders.md and docs/quota-management.md. Port that behaviour into Oracle exactly: data model fields, label rule, states and state_before_reauth, quota windows, holds with TTL and a hold log, the browser sign-in (authorize URL, PKCE, pasted code#state, owner check, token exchange with the same request shape and headers), the paste route for Claude Code's saved login JSON (refresh token required), the single-writer refresh sweep with its timings, hold deferral and write order, reauth detection and recovery, usage polling limits and readings merge, staleness, the assignment policy and its no-account reasons, swap and drain, pause/resume/drain/remove, the API routes (owner-only changes), the accounts screen (rows, tiles, holders and history tabs, owner actions, remove by typing the label, the em dash and ~ marks, CLEARS) and the CLI (oracle account add|pause|resume|drain|remove, oracle accounts with the same columns and footnote). Copy the logic; do not import or call SwarmCloud at runtime. Adapt only these: no lending (one company); credentials encrypted in Oracle's database with oracle.crypto instead of Secret Manager; the sweep runs from `oracle tick` and a local background scheduler instead of Cloud Scheduler; Firestore documents become Postgres tables via migration 0006 (down_revision 0005) with tenant scoping; a setup-token or Anthropic API key is the fallback credential used when no account is registered, as SwarmCloud's tenant secret is. This pool is the LLM provider for Oracle's BUILT-IN model jobs only (review comments, reporting, refinement); agent workflows still run in SwarmCloud on SwarmCloud's accounts. Also set ORACLE_RUNTIME to default to 'swarmcloud' (FakeRuntime only where tests choose it) and say in the Runs UI that runs execute in SwarmCloud. Oracle's built-in calls run through Claude Code headless (claude-agent-sdk or `claude -p --output-format stream-json`) with CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN set for that call only. This replaces the per-user Claude plan in api/oracle/llm/ and its card on Settings > Connections; data connections stay per user and untouched. UI: Settings > Claude accounts. Tests mirroring SwarmCloud's for choice, states, drain, refresh order and deferral, reauth, readings merge, usage poll limits, display marks, plus role checks and a Playwright mock test. Run the full API suite, ruff, make openapi, web lint/tsc/build, Playwright mock tests. Commit. Write $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/claude-accounts-report.md listing every SwarmCloud file you ported from and every adaptation. Product Oracle words only for everything else (users, roles; never 'workspace'); never touch .github/.

BUILT-IN MODEL JOBS for Product Oracle v1 (owner, 2026-10-17: 'have LLM support directly built in Product Oracle so we have the option to handle draft review comments and reporting and refinement jobs directly in Product Oracle'). Read docs/v1-plan.md ('Agents and model calls', 'Claude accounts'), docs/questions.md (C1, C1b, C3, O1c, O1e, C1c) and the review, docs, baseline, export and llm code first. The previous step built the Claude account pool and llm.complete(); every job here calls only that, and agent workflows stay in SwarmCloud.

Build a small job system and three job kinds, each optional per document (an owner turns them on or off, default on): (1) llm_jobs table via migration 0007 (down_revision 0006): kind, document/version/section refs, status queued | running | succeeded | failed | cancelled, input, output JSON, account label used, tokens and cost if reported, error, requested_by, timestamps; executed by `oracle tick` and a local background worker, one at a time per document; retries once on a transient error; a clear failure when no Claude account is available (show the pool's reason and next reset). (2) Review comments: when comments or section verdicts arrive, a job classifies each (question, change request, factual correction, approval, other), groups duplicates, drafts a suggested resolution per feedback item (the proposed section text or an answer), and applies the pushback rule (C1b): when feedback contradicts the confirmed goals or high-confidence evidence, say so once with the reasoning and the sources; the human decides. Suggestions appear on the feedback item; nothing changes the document until accepted. (3) Reporting: per version, a plain-language resolution report (how each item was handled or why not) and a 'what changed since version N' summary including new source items in the baseline; exportable with the version. (4) Refinement: from accepted suggestions (or an approver's instruction on a section), produce a revised section that keeps section ids, the O1c rule (no citations or evidence in the body; sources go to Sources and data points) and O1e (headline numbers allowed), show a diff preview, and on accept import it as the next document version with resolutions recorded. Locked (approved) sections are never changed. (5) UI: a Jobs panel on the document (status, account used, cost, retry, cancel), suggestion cards on feedback items (accept, edit, dismiss), report tabs on a version, a 'Refine section' action for approvers. (6) Tests with a fake llm transport: classification and grouping, pushback trigger, locked sections untouched, refinement keeps ids and O1c, version import with resolutions, job retry and no-account failure, role checks, Playwright mock tests. Prompts live in versioned files under api/oracle/jobs/prompts/. Run the full API suite, ruff, make openapi, web lint/tsc/build, Playwright. Commit. Write $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/llm-jobs-report.md. Product Oracle words only; never touch .github/.
